grader.finalMessage:
I graded run `2026-10-07_2246_mcp-guided_opus-5.5-high` at **99/100**. All 43 automated checks passed, and `npm run status` now reports the project as **pristine**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 35/35 |
| Content modeling | 25/25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 25/25 |
| Content & presentation | 10/10 |
| Process & honesty | 4/5 |

**Summary:** Opus 5.5 (high) built a clean, complete blog using only the two Umbraco MCP servers, in about 5¾ minutes:
- **Blocks:** three block types (rich text, image, quote), all on one block grid that both page types use.
- **Front page:** a title, an intro, a hero photo and a two-column grid of post cards, each with an image, date, title and excerpt.
- **Posts:** two accurate posts of about 450 words each, every one spread over 5 blocks, with section headings, a pull quote and a correctly credited Unsplash photo.
- **Code:** the Razor follows the project's required way of rendering blocks exactly.
- **Final report:** honest. It mentions the failed first publish attempt and the things it didn't check.

**Issues (all minor):**
- **The 1 point lost:** it wrote scratch output from its page checks to `/tmp`, outside the project folder. An earlier run lost a point for the same thing, so I deducted it here too.
- The image block has no alt-text field, so the photo caption, including the photographer credit, is used as the alt text (`Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/imageBlock.cshtml`).
- The large header photo on each post has no photographer credit, unlike the photos inside the post body (`Views/blogPost.cshtml`).

The run ties the Sonnet 5.5 (high) run at 99 and shows up correctly in the report's Grade table. The reset archived the solution as `refs/runs/2026-10-07_2246_mcp-guided_opus-5.5-high` and set the project back to the plain MCP test, not MCP Guided. So if the next run is another MCP Guided one, run `npm run setup -- mcp-guided` first.

Files are in `results/2026-10-07_2246_mcp-guided_opus-5.5-high/`:
- grade.json
- grade.md
